detail: D-20260927-01 - Ship the app as a DMG installer instead of a zip
D-20260929-01 - Lint and format with clippy, rustfmt, ESLint and Prettier; licence header on every source file
release build from a clean target fails: dlopen of proc-macro dylib: mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool; then E0463 can't find crate for thiserror_impl / serde_derive
error: release build from a clean target fails: dlopen of proc-macro dylib: mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool; then E0463 can't find crate for thiserror_impl / serde_derive
fix: [profile.release.build-override] strip = false in src-tauri/Cargo.toml; the shipped binary is still stripped.
root_cause: profile.release strip = true also applies to proc macros and build scripts (build-override inherits strip); Xcode 27's strip leaves those dylibs in a form dyld refuses to load. An existing target hid it until cargo clean.

detail: whole-disk scan total larger than the disk's used space; CoreSpotlight shown at ~250 GB while du says ~60 GB
error: whole-disk scan total larger than the disk's used space; CoreSpotlight shown at ~250 GB while du says ~60 GB
fix: Progress keeps a (dev, ino) set for files with nlink > 1; only the first link met adds bytes, later links still count as files. Tests for hard links and for symlinks not being followed.
root_cause: walk summed st_blocks for every directory entry, so a file with several hard links was counted once per link. Spotlight's journals are linked into up to ten folders each.

detail: D-20260929-02 - Free space drawn only at the top of a whole-volume scan
Clicking a folder with thousands of files hangs the app
error: Clicking a folder with thousands of files hangs the app
fix: FileTable renders PAGE (120) rows and appends a page when the scroll container nears its bottom; a layout effect keeps adding until the list scrolls; the count is keyed to the rows array so filter/sort/new path reset it
root_cause: FileTable rendered a <tr> for every file in one React commit, so layout of thousands of rows blocked the main thread; the Rust listing was already fast and off-thread
